item.text: {"question_id":"7B.1","answer":"The record is mixed, with a materially adverse pattern in public truthfulness during the 2022–2023 period. López Obrador publicly denied or minimized military Pegasus surveillance and rejected the GIEI’s Ayotzinapa findings, while the supplied reporting described documentary, forensic, or investigative evidence contradicting those positions (BATCH-0005-E005; BATCH-0009-E007). Fact-checkers classified substantial portions of his government-report and press-conference claims as false or misleading, including claims defending his government, but these classifications establish inaccurate or contested statements rather than subjective knowledge or deliberate deception (BATCH-0042-E009; BATCH-0043-E009). His attacks on journalists and organizations reporting on spyware allegations are directly documented, though the causal link to resulting threats is not independently adjudicated in the supplied material (BATCH-0029-E006). Qualifying evidence includes his acknowledgment that leaked health records were accurate, his apology for prematurely disclosing a central-bank decision, and his stated willingness to order reviews of family-related allegations (BATCH-0044-E008; BATCH-0048-E003; BATCH-0042-E001). Overall, the evidence supports repeated inaccurate, defensive, and reputation-protective statements, but does not establish that every false or misleading claim was knowingly deceptive or that López Obrador personally ordered the underlying surveillance or
